To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CD68+ and/orCD163+ tumor-associated infiltrating macrophage infiltration, and crown-like structures (adipose tissue lesions with macrophage accumulation) are associated with clinicopathological parameters of human breast cancer.

CD68+ and/orCD163+ macrophage infiltration, as well as CLSS, are present in mammary adipocytes nearby the breast cancer, and that these are related to various clinicopathologic factors of breast cancer.
tumor-associated macrophages are present in mammary adipocytes and are associated with the clinicopathologic parameters and the prognosis of breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the presence and significance of tumor-associated macrophages in breast adipose tissue.
the role of adipose tissue in the progression of breast cancer, and provides a basis for future studies.
the presence of macrophage infiltration in the adipose tissue of breast cancer and its association with various clinicopathological features of breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tumor associated macrophages and/or CLSs in adipose tissue of the breast are associated with various clinical parameters of breast cancer, but their prognostic significance is still unclear.
tumor-associated macrophages in mammary adipocyte tissue are associated with poor clinical outcomes in breast cancer.
tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are associated with poor clinical outcomes in breast cancer, and that CLSs are associated with poor prognosis in node-positive breast cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD163+ macro-phages and CD163+ CLs in breast adipose tissue may serve as a potential prognostic factor for node-negative and node-positive breast cancer, respectively.
the presence of tumor-associated macrophages within adipose tissue is a potential prognostic marker in breast cancer.
CD68+ and/or CLSs are associated with poor prognosis of breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD163+ macro-phages and CLS may serve as a novel biomarker for breast cancer prognosis.
tumor-associated macrophages may play a role in the development of breast cancer.
